summary: A pragmatic ML training data platform that treats shards as immutable objects and uses versioned manifests as the commit boundary, pushing the hot read path directly to object storage with range reads and SDK-side caching. The design is largely production-credible, with clean separation of control/data planes and sensible failure-mode handling, but it needs more rigor around large-scale metadata growth, garbage collection, and immutability enforcement.
strengths: Strong commit semantics via an explicit STAGING→COMMITTED transaction boundary, enabling deterministic, auditable dataset versions under massive fan-out
Sound scalability direction by offloading durability/replication to object storage and putting performance-critical behaviors (range-read coalescing, retries/hedging, node-local cache) in the SDK
weaknesses: Metadata and ingest flow may bottleneck at scale (per-shard RegisterObject calls, large objects table growth, missing batching/partitioning/backpressure and practical limits on version sizes)

Operational gaps around lifecycle and integrity (GC/orphan cleanup for aborted versions, enforcing immutability/object-lock or content-addressed keys, multi-region strategy and cache eviction/consistency details)
